description: Lightning courts its antlers. It stands on the high fells in the worst weather, daring the sky to try.
lore: Go up the high fells in filthy weather and there it is, planted where the ground runs out, facing down into the wind with the summit at its back. Lightning comes to the antlers the way pigeons come to a sill. It does not shy and it does not lie down, and the white of its eye is the brightest thing on the mountain. Whatever it is doing it has been doing since before anyone thought to count, and there is nobody in there to leave off doing it.

A woman climbs up to stand near it. Different weather, same stag, five or six times a year. Standing near it in a storm is how you get broken — the bolt takes the antlers or it takes you — and what is left of you re-forms beside the nearest tended fire some hours later, short a little of what you were thinking.

The nearest tended fire is [[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]]'s, out on the meadow, a long walk from those fells, and the walk is the point: she gets the whole way back to notice what she has put down. Solveig has met her nine times. She does the courtesy every time — sits with her, tells her what has happened to her, asks her name and one true thing. The name still comes. The one true thing is shorter each time. Solveig asked her once what she goes up there for. She said: because he does not flinch, and I want to see how it is done.
gm_notes: Shipped description adopted verbatim — 'daring the sky to try' is exactly the art (huge planted bull, pale rack, white eyes, blue arcs off antlers and hocks) and the record's whole job is to complicate it. The stag is stage Habit: what reads as defiance is a behaviour with nobody home, and it should never be given a motive on the page. The climber is the record. Being broken costs you a little of what you were thinking (root, Law III), so she is using the mountain to unload something, deliberately, at the rate of five or six times a year, and Solveig — who cannot leave the fire and would not anyway — receives her each time and performs the courtesy on a woman actively spending herself. Do not name what she is trying to put down, and do not let a player fix her; the only lever anyone has is Solveig's, which is to keep asking her name.
